What the study asks:
Here, we used 23 years of observations on co-flowering synchrony among 142 animal pollinated plant species in three common dryland ecosystems of the southwest USA to address, (1) Which climate variables best predict co-flowering synchrony, and are climate predictors generalizable across ecosystem types? We then paired flowering phenology with 18 years of co-located monthly abundance data for 88 bee species to evaluate, (2) Does the seasonal stability of bees track co-flowering synchrony independent of climate, and does this relationship differ between specialists and generalists? Finally, we used long-term trends to ask, (3) Has synchrony changed over time and consistently among ecosystems?

Qs addressed in this script:
Q3: change in synchrony over time and Q1: climate predictors of synchrony 

Reads the synchrony file written by `01_synchrony_calculation.Rmd`.

## Co-flowering overlap over time
Has synchrony changed over time and consistently among ecosystems?
Because transect is the true unit of replication, for this analysis we implement a two stage approach.
First we estimate a slope using least-squares regression of co-flowering synchrony over time at each
transect, then test whether overall those slopes differ from zero, and whether the slopes differ by what site the transects are within.

We then do a sensitivity analysis by down-weighting imprecise slope estimates by 1/ the slopes SE.

### Prepare data
 load in the co-flowering data from above and calculate average co-flowering overlap
```{r}
#change to your working dir
setwd("~/Documents/co-flowering synchrony/Updated 10:23:26")

# Load co-flowering data
overlap <- read.csv("data/plant_plant_overlapthru2024.csv")
overlap <- overlap %>%
  filter(!site %in% c("J", "P", "JSAV"))

overlap$site <- as.factor(overlap$site)
overlap$species.x <- as.factor(overlap$species.x)
overlap$species.y <- as.factor(overlap$species.y)

# Calculate yearly average overlap for each transect
# Summarize yearly overlap per site per web_id over time
overlap <- overlap %>%
  dplyr:: group_by(site, year, web) %>%
  dplyr:: summarise(
    mean_overlap = mean(overlap, na.rm = TRUE),
    se_overlap = sd(overlap, na.rm = TRUE)/sqrt(n())
  ) %>%
  dplyr:: ungroup()
#once averaged mean overlap is still ~0.6
summary(overlap)

# Shared figure labels/colors (defined here so every figure chunk can use them,
# regardless of figure order). Colors come from 00_setup (ms_site_colors).
site_colors    <- ms_site_colors   # B=#2c6c9c, G=#8a8a8a, C=#5f7d33
site_labels    <- c("G" = "Desert grassland", "B" = "Plains grassland", "C" = "Desert shrubland")
site_labels_pm <- c("B" = "Plains~grassland", "G" = "Desert~grassland", "C" = "Desert~shrubland")
```

Load climate data and merge with co-flowering data
```{r}
# Load climate data (need to call dplyr)
PDO <- read.csv("data/pdo.timeseries.ersstv5.csv") %>% filter (year > 1998) %>% 
  dplyr:: group_by(year) %>% 
  dplyr:: summarize(mean(PDO)) %>% 
  dplyr:: rename(annual.PDO = `mean(PDO)`)
precip <- read.csv("data/climatebyyear_updated.csv")
climate <-  merge(precip, PDO, by = "year", all.y = TRUE)
climate$annual.precip <- climate$season.precip.fall + climate$season.precip.spring 

# Assign met stations
overlap <- overlap %>%
  mutate(met_station = case_when(
    site %in% c("G", "C") ~ "met49",
    site == "B" ~ "met50"))

climate <- climate %>%
  dplyr::rename(met_station = site)

# Merge climate data with co-flowering data 
overlap <- merge(
  overlap,
  climate,
  by.x = c("year", "met_station"),
  by.y = c("year", "met_station"),
  all.x = TRUE) 

# add 2001 PDO back in for met50 2001 rows
overlap$annual.PDO[overlap$met_station == "met50" & overlap$year == 2001] <- -0.7419167

# Change web to web_id to make unique transect identifier (needed for AR models)
overlap <- overlap %>%
  mutate(web_id = interaction(site, web)) %>% 
  mutate(site = factor(site, levels = c("B", "G", "C"))) 

# Remove rows where se = NA, indicating only one overlap value
# Confirmed that this is the case to 2003 creosote outlier
overlap <- overlap %>% drop_na(se_overlap)

write.csv(overlap, "data/plant_overlap_climate_filtered.csv", row.names = FALSE)

#to read file back in, uncomment line below
#overlap<- read.csv("data/plant_overlap_climate_filtered.csv")
```

### 1.1 Change in synchrony over time (ALL SITES)
```{r}
#Filtering out any transects that do not have at least 5 years of data-- cannot get a 
# decent slope estimate on too little data
transect_years <- overlap %>% dplyr::distinct(site, web_id, year) %>%
  dplyr::count(site, web_id, name = "n_years")
keep_transects <- dplyr::filter(transect_years, n_years >= 5)

#joining back with filtered transects and scaling year so slope estimates dont start
#at year 0
overlap_s <- overlap %>%
  dplyr::semi_join(keep_transects, by = c("site", "web_id")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year_scaled = as.numeric(scale(year)))
# -> 12 transects: Stage 2a global = F_{1,11}; 2b/2c site = df 9

# ---- Stage 1: one temporal slope per transect (least-squares) ----
web_slopes_year <- overlap_s %>%
  group_by(site, web_id) %>%
  do(tidy(lm(mean_overlap ~ year_scaled, data = .))) %>%
  filter(term == "year_scaled") %>%
  ungroup()
#all of our slopes, by transect and site, with their SE
print(web_slopes_year)

# ---- Stage 2a: GLOBAL trend (intercept-only = one-sample t-test of mean slope vs 0) ----
global_year_model <- lm(estimate ~ 1, data = web_slopes_year)
summary(global_year_model)
# mean slope = +0.0128, t_{11} = 2.12, p = 0.058  -> synchrony has a positive slope, but
# not strong evidence it is increasing over time, pooled across sites

# ---- Stage 2b: do site slopes DIFFER? (joint 2-df test, not reducible to a single t) ----
site_year_model <- lm(estimate ~ site, data = web_slopes_year)
anova(site_year_model)   # F_{2,9}=12.25 P = 0.002 There is an among-ecosystem difference in mean transect slope!

# ---- PER-SITE trend (intercept model per site: each site's mean slope vs 0) ----
# `~ 0 + site` drops the global intercept so each coefficient = that site's mean slope,
# each t-tested against zero (pooled residual SE, df = 9).
site_trends <- lm(estimate ~ 0 + site, data = web_slopes_year)
summary(site_trends)
# B = negative/flat (non significant), G = positive, C = positive 
#       Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
#siteB -0.009341   0.005999  -1.557 0.153876    
#siteG  0.032436   0.005999   5.407 0.000429 ***
#siteC  0.015275   0.005999   2.546 0.031381 * 

# ---- Stage 2 (weighted robustness): down-weight imprecise transect slopes by 1/SE ----
global_year_w <- lm(estimate ~ 1,        weights = 1/std.error, data = web_slopes_year)
summary(global_year_w)                              # weighted global trend
site_year_w   <- lm(estimate ~ site,     weights = 1/std.error, data = web_slopes_year)
anova(site_year_w)                                  # weighted among-site difference
site_trends_w <- lm(estimate ~ 0 + site, weights = 1/std.error, data = web_slopes_year)
summary(site_trends_w)                              # weighted per-site trends

#all weighted trends are roughly similar to unweighted trends. Except, site C flips from P =0.03 to 0.05, so not strong evidence that slope is not just noise. 
####### Site G is the only reliable increase over time ###########

# ---- Richness check: is the synchrony trend a species-count artifact? ----
rich_ty   <- read.csv("data/richness_by_transectyear.csv")
overlap_r <- overlap_s %>% dplyr::left_join(rich_ty, by = c("year","site","web"))
summary(overlap_r$n_species)                        # must NOT be all-NA

# does richness itself trend over time?
summary(lm(n_species ~ year_scaled, data = overlap_r))   
# richness does not change over time
```

## Co-flowering overlap & Climate

### Synchrony & Climate (ALL SITES) 

We want to determine the climate predictor that best tracks co-flowering synchrony
We first test our candidate set of climate predictors for temporal autocorrelation
then use AICc to determine the best fitting models for synchrony ~ climate, both
linear and non-linear quadratic, as plant responses to climate are often nonlinear

MODEL SELECTION 1 - Temporal Autocorrelation
* Find best autocorrelation using linear model
* Next step uses best AR model to test non-linear models 
```{r}
oc <- overlap[!is.na(overlap$season.precip.spring) & !is.na(overlap$annual.PDO), ]
oc$year_fact <- as.factor(oc$year)

# FALL/MONSOON PRECIP
lm_overlap_fall_precip     <- lme(mean_overlap ~ season.precip.fall * site, random = ~1|web_id, method = "ML", data = oc, na.action = na.omit)
lm_overlap_fall_precip_AR1 <- lme(mean_overlap ~ season.precip.fall * site, random = ~1|web_id, method = "ML", correlation = corAR1(form = ~year|web_id), data = oc, na.action = na.omit)
lm_overlap_fall_precip_AR2 <- lme(mean_overlap ~ season.precip.fall * site, random = ~1|web_id, method = "ML", correlation = corARMA(form = ~year|web_id, p = 2), data = oc, na.action = na.omit)

#using MuMIn AICc function- gives second order akaike information criterion
AICc(lm_overlap_fall_precip, lm_overlap_fall_precip_AR1, lm_overlap_fall_precip_AR2)

# SPRING PRECIP
lm_overlap_spring_precip     <- lme(mean_overlap ~ season.precip.spring * site, random = ~1|web_id, method = "ML", data = oc, na.action = na.omit)
lm_overlap_spring_precip_AR1 <- lme(mean_overlap ~ season.precip.spring * site, random = ~1|web_id, method = "ML", correlation = corAR1(form = ~year|web_id), data = oc, na.action = na.omit)
lm_overlap_spring_precip_AR2 <- lme(mean_overlap ~ season.precip.spring * site, random = ~1|web_id, method = "ML", correlation = corARMA(form = ~ year|web_id, p = 2), data = oc, na.action = na.omit)

AICc(lm_overlap_spring_precip, lm_overlap_spring_precip_AR1, lm_overlap_spring_precip_AR2)

# ANNUAL PRECIP
lm_overlap_annual_precip     <- lme(mean_overlap ~ annual.precip * site, random = ~1|web_id, method = "ML", data = oc, na.action = na.omit)
lm_overlap_annual_precip_AR1 <- lme(mean_overlap ~ annual.precip * site, random = ~1|web_id, method = "ML", correlation = corAR1(form = ~year|web_id), data = oc, na.action = na.omit)
lm_overlap_annual_precip_AR2 <- lme(mean_overlap ~ annual.precip * site, random = ~1|web_id, method = "ML", correlation = corARMA(form = ~year|web_id, p = 2), data = oc, na.action = na.omit)

AICc(lm_overlap_annual_precip, lm_overlap_annual_precip_AR1, lm_overlap_annual_precip_AR2)

# COOL-SEASON TEMPERATURE (GDD.spring)
lm_overlap_gdd_spring     <- lme(mean_overlap ~ GDD.spring * site, random = ~1|web_id, method = "ML", data = oc, na.action = na.omit)
lm_overlap_gdd_spring_AR1 <- lme(mean_overlap ~ GDD.spring * site, random = ~1|web_id, method = "ML", correlation = corAR1(form = ~year|web_id), data = oc, na.action = na.omit)
lm_overlap_gdd_spring_AR2 <- lme(mean_overlap ~ GDD.spring * site, random = ~1|web_id, method = "ML", correlation = corARMA(form = ~year|web_id, p = 2), data = oc, na.action = na.omit)

AICc(lm_overlap_gdd_spring, lm_overlap_gdd_spring_AR1, lm_overlap_gdd_spring_AR2)

# WARM-SEASON TEMPERATURE (GDD.fall)
lm_overlap_gdd_fall     <- lme(mean_overlap ~ GDD.fall * site, random = ~1|web_id, method = "ML", data = oc, na.action = na.omit)
lm_overlap_gdd_fall_AR1 <- lme(mean_overlap ~ GDD.fall * site, random = ~1|web_id, method = "ML", correlation = corAR1(form = ~year|web_id), data = oc, na.action = na.omit)
lm_overlap_gdd_fall_AR2 <- lme(mean_overlap ~ GDD.fall * site, random = ~1|web_id, method = "ML", correlation = corARMA(form = ~year|web_id, p = 2), data = oc, na.action = na.omit)

AICc(lm_overlap_gdd_fall, lm_overlap_gdd_fall_AR1, lm_overlap_gdd_fall_AR2)

# PDO 
lm_overlap_PDO     <- lme(mean_overlap ~ annual.PDO * site, random = ~1|web_id, method = "ML", data = oc, na.action = na.omit)
lm_overlap_PDO_AR1 <- lme(mean_overlap ~ annual.PDO * site, random = ~1|web_id, method = "ML", correlation = corAR1(form = ~year|web_id), data = oc, na.action = na.omit)
lm_overlap_PDO_AR2 <- lme(mean_overlap ~ annual.PDO * site, random = ~1|web_id, method = "ML", correlation = corARMA(form = ~year|web_id, p = 2), data = oc, na.action = na.omit)

AICc(lm_overlap_PDO, lm_overlap_PDO_AR1, lm_overlap_PDO_AR2)
#only PDO clears deta AICc of at least 2. AR1 is delta AICc 3 more than non AR model.

#only for PDO does AR improve model fit, will move forward with AR1 for PDO
```

MODEL SELECTION 2 - Non-linear fits using best models from above
Since almost none of the above best models had temporal autocorrelation, we opted to swap to lmer
```{r}
vars <- c("mean_overlap", "site", "web_id", "year",
          "season.precip.fall", "season.precip.spring", "annual.precip",
          "annual.PDO", "GDD.spring", "GDD.fall")
oc_cc <- oc[complete.cases(oc[, vars]), ]

# --- Scale predictors prior to modeling (z-scores; response left raw)
oc_cc$fall_precip_z   <- as.numeric(scale(oc_cc$season.precip.fall))
oc_cc$spring_precip_z <- as.numeric(scale(oc_cc$season.precip.spring))
oc_cc$annual_precip_z <- as.numeric(scale(oc_cc$annual.precip))
oc_cc$PDO_z           <- as.numeric(scale(oc_cc$annual.PDO))
oc_cc$GDD_spring_z    <- as.numeric(scale(oc_cc$GDD.spring))
oc_cc$GDD_fall_z      <- as.numeric(scale(oc_cc$GDD.fall))

# year must be integer & unique within web_id for corAR1
oc_cc$year <- as.integer(oc_cc$year)

# WARM-SEASON / MONSOON precip (season.precip.fall)
lm_overlap_fall_precip  <- lmer(mean_overlap ~ fall_precip_z * site + (1 | web_id),
                                data = oc_cc, REML = FALSE)
lm_overlap_fall_precip2 <- lmer(mean_overlap ~ poly(fall_precip_z, 2) * site + (1 | web_id),
                                data = oc_cc, REML = FALSE)

# COOL-SEASON precip
lm_overlap_spring_precip  <- lmer(mean_overlap ~ spring_precip_z * site + (1 | web_id),
                                  data = oc_cc, REML = FALSE)
lm_overlap_spring_precip2 <- lmer(mean_overlap ~ poly(spring_precip_z, 2) * site + (1 | web_id),
                                  data = oc_cc, REML = FALSE)

# Annual precip
lm_overlap_annual_precip  <- lmer(mean_overlap ~ annual_precip_z * site + (1 | web_id),
                                  data = oc_cc, REML = FALSE)
lm_overlap_annual_precip2 <- lmer(mean_overlap ~ poly(annual_precip_z, 2) * site + (1 | web_id),
                                  data = oc_cc, REML = FALSE)

# PDO (AR1 strongly supported; lmer can't fit AR1, so stays in nlme)
lm_overlap_PDO  <- lme(mean_overlap ~ PDO_z * site, random = ~1 | web_id,
                       correlation = corAR1(form = ~ year | web_id),
                       method = "ML", data = oc_cc, na.action = na.omit)
lm_overlap_PDO2 <- lme(mean_overlap ~ poly(PDO_z, 2) * site, random = ~1 | web_id,
                       correlation = corAR1(form = ~ year | web_id),
                       method = "ML", data = oc_cc, na.action = na.omit)

# Temperature candidates (growing degree days)
m_gdd_spring  <- lmer(mean_overlap ~ GDD_spring_z * site + (1 | web_id),
                      data = oc_cc, REML = FALSE)
m_gdd_spring2 <- lmer(mean_overlap ~ poly(GDD_spring_z, 2) * site + (1 | web_id),
                      data = oc_cc, REML = FALSE)
m_gdd_fall    <- lmer(mean_overlap ~ GDD_fall_z * site + (1 | web_id),
                      data = oc_cc, REML = FALSE)
m_gdd_fall2   <- lmer(mean_overlap ~ poly(GDD_fall_z, 2) * site + (1 | web_id),
                      data = oc_cc, REML = FALSE)

# --- AICc comparison 
AICc(lm_overlap_fall_precip,   lm_overlap_fall_precip2,
            lm_overlap_spring_precip, lm_overlap_spring_precip2,
            lm_overlap_annual_precip, lm_overlap_annual_precip2,
            lm_overlap_PDO,           lm_overlap_PDO2,
            m_gdd_spring,             m_gdd_spring2,
            m_gdd_fall,               m_gdd_fall2)

#spring precip 2 wins with dAICc 14 to next best model with is linear PDO, dAICc to next best is 4 which is quadratic PDO
```

Results from the best model (cool-season precip, quadratic)
```{r}
options(contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly"))  # Type III w/ interactions

oc_cc <- dplyr::left_join(oc_cc, rich_ty, by = c("year", "site", "web"))
summary(oc_cc$n_species)     

## COOL-SEASON (SPRING) PRECIP, quadratic model ######
cool_model <- lmer(mean_overlap ~ poly(spring_precip_z, 2) * site + (1 | web_id),
                                  data = oc_cc, REML = FALSE)
anova(cool_model, type = 3)
#                                   Sum Sq Mean Sq NumDF   DenDF F value    Pr(>F)    
#poly(season.precip.spring, 2)      1.25352 0.62676     2 242.569 41.7771 2.566e-16 ***
#site                               0.05206 0.02603     2   2.746  1.7352    0.3257    
#poly(season.precip.spring, 2):site 0.04051 0.01013     4 242.599  0.6751    0.6098   

qqnorm(resid(cool_model)); qqline(resid(cool_model)); hist(resid(cool_model))

## does richness confound this effect?
cool_model_rich <- lmer(mean_overlap ~ poly(spring_precip_z, 2) * site +  n_species + (1 | web_id), data = oc_cc, REML = FALSE)
anova(cool_model_rich, type = 3)
#                               Sum Sq Mean Sq NumDF   DenDF F value    Pr(>F)    
#poly(spring_precip_z, 2)      0.84019 0.42010     2 279.810 29.4415 2.488e-12 ***
#site                          0.33689 0.16845     2   9.949 11.8053  0.002362 ** 
#n_species                     0.30544 0.30544     1 166.085 21.4059 7.448e-06 ***
#poly(spring_precip_z, 2):site 0.06011 0.01503     4 270.789  1.0532  0.380147  

#richness predicts synchrony with F of 21 and P of 0.00
AICc(cool_model, cool_model_rich)
#including richness wins by dAICc of 18. including it in the model does not negate the effect of spring precip on synchrony, howevver
# ---- Marginal (R2m) and conditional (R2c) R-squared
MuMIn::r.squaredGLMM(cool_model)            # climate only  (R2m = fixed effects)
MuMIn::r.squaredGLMM(cool_model_rich)       # climate + richness
#R2m is 0.23 for richness blind model, is 0.29 for richness incld model, it improves fit, but not by a massive margin

#### PDO model ##### 
pdo_model <- lme(mean_overlap ~ PDO_z * site, random = ~1 | web_id,
                       correlation = corAR1(form = ~ year | web_id),
                       method = "ML", data = oc_cc, na.action = na.omit)

anova(pdo_model, type = "marginal")   # nlme's Type III equivalent
#                    numDF denDF   F-value p-value
#(Intercept)             1   269 2491.0873  <.0001
#poly(PDO_z, 2)          2   269   35.7768  <.0001
#site                    2    12    2.3782  0.1349
#poly(PDO_z, 2):site     4   269    1.0518  0.3809

qqnorm(resid(pdo_model)); qqline(resid(pdo_model)); hist(resid(pdo_model))

## does richness confund this effect?
pdo_model_rich <- lme(mean_overlap ~ PDO_z * site + n_species, random = ~1 | web_id,
                       correlation = corAR1(form = ~ year | web_id),
                       method = "ML", data = oc_cc, na.action = na.omit)

anova(pdo_model_rich, type = "marginal")  
#            numDF denDF  F-value p-value
#Intercept)     1   271 735.1198  <.0001
#PDO_z           1   271  47.3804  <.0001
#site            2    12  11.9441  0.0014
#n_species       1   271  33.0013  <.0001
#PDO_z:site      2   271   1.0338  0.3571

#richness again does not kill the PDO effect

AICc(pdo_model, pdo_model_rich)
#richness model has better fit by dAICc of 30, so pretty substantial

# ---- Marginal (R2m) and conditional (R2c) R-squared ----
MuMIn::r.squaredGLMM(pdo_model)            # climate only  (R2m = fixed effects)
MuMIn::r.squaredGLMM(pdo_model_rich)     # climate + richness
# R2m is 0.15 for rich blind model and 0.23 for rich incld, so it improves fit but not by such a wide margin

#so for both the cool season precip and PDO effect, richness adds information to the model, it is explaining variance in synchrony. But, it does not kill the effect of our climate predictors, but does explain some added variance 
```

##inferene from best climate models
```{r}
mean_syn <- mean(oc_cc$mean_overlap, na.rm = TRUE)
mean_syn

## ---------- COOL-SEASON PRECIP (quadratic) ----------
cool_model <- lmer(mean_overlap ~ poly(season.precip.spring, 2) * site + (1 | web_id),
                   data = oc_cc, REML = TRUE)        # REML for inference

# predicted synchrony across the observed precip range, pooled over site
sp_grid <- seq(min(oc_cc$season.precip.spring, na.rm = TRUE),
               max(oc_cc$season.precip.spring, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = 2000)
em_cool <- as.data.frame(emmeans(cool_model, ~ season.precip.spring,
                                  at = list(season.precip.spring = sp_grid)))

em_cool[which.max(em_cool$emmean), ]  # precip where synchrony is highest
em_cool[which.min(em_cool$emmean), ]  # precip (mm) where synchrony is lowest
em_cool[c(1, nrow(em_cool)), ]        # synchrony at lowest & highest precip

#goes from 0.6 syn at 0mm precip, down to 0.36 at 70 mm, up to 0.44 at 109 mm

# polynomial refit: gives beta (linear) & gamma (quadratic).
# Pooled over site (interaction n.s.)
cool_raw <- lmer(mean_overlap ~ poly(season.precip.spring, 2, raw = TRUE) + (1 | web_id),
                 data = oc_cc, REML = TRUE)

summary(cool_raw)$coefficients        # estimate, SE, df, t, p for intercept, beta, gamma
confint(cool_raw, method = "Wald")    # 95% CIs

b     <- fixef(cool_raw)
beta  <- b[2]   # linear term
gamma <- b[3]   # quadratic term
# turning point (vertex): precip where synchrony is min/max
vertex <- -beta / (2 * gamma); vertex
#the vertex, where it turns up, is at 72 mm precip, convex function with a steep decline
# from 0mm to ~70mm and then a slight increase up to ~100mm

## ---------- PDO (linear) ----------
pdo_model <- lme(mean_overlap ~ annual.PDO * site, random = ~1 | web_id,
                 correlation = corAR1(form = ~ year | web_id),
                 method = "REML", data = oc_cc, na.action = na.omit)

emtrends(pdo_model, ~ 1, var = "annual.PDO")# synchrony change per PDO unit + 95% CI
#      annual.PDO.trend    SE  df lower.CL upper.CL
# overall          -0.0672 0.008 272  -0.0829  -0.0515
#syn decreases by ~0.07 for every unit increase in PDO 

pdo_slope <- summary(emtrends(pdo_model, ~ 1, var = "annual.PDO"))$annual.PDO.trend

pdo_slope / mean_syn * 100  # % of mean synchrony 
pdo_slope * diff(range(oc_cc$annual.PDO, na.rm = TRUE)) # absolute swing across observed PDO range
pdo_slope * diff(range(oc_cc$annual.PDO, na.rm = TRUE)) / mean_syn * 100 # that swing as % of mean
#synchrony declines by 40% of its mean across the observed range of PDO values
pdo_rng <- range(oc_cc$annual.PDO, na.rm = TRUE)   # observed min & max PDO

em_pdo <- as.data.frame(emmeans(pdo_model, ~ annual.PDO,
                                at = list(annual.PDO = pdo_rng)))
em_pdo   # predicted synchrony at lowest & highest PDO, averaged over site, with 95% CIs
#at minumum observed annual PDO (-1.8), syn is ~0.5. At maximum observed PDO (0.8) syn is ~0.36.
#annual.PDO    emmean         SE df  lower.CL  upper.CL
# -1.8821667 0.5409548 0.01721313 14 0.5040363 0.5778732
#  0.8053333 0.3603531 0.01710162 14 0.3236738 0.3970324
```

## Figure 2: Synchrony vs cool-season precipitation and PDO
```{r}

# ---- Figure models (no site term: pooled fit) ----
cool_model_fig <- lmer(mean_overlap ~ poly(season.precip.spring, 2) + (1 | web_id),
                       data = oc, REML = TRUE)

pdo_model_fig <- lme(mean_overlap ~ annual.PDO,
                     random = ~1 | web_id,
                     correlation = corAR1(form = ~ year | web_id),
                     method = "REML", data = oc, na.action = na.omit)

# ---- (A) Cool-season precip (quadratic) ----
sp_grid <- seq(min(oc$season.precip.spring, na.rm = TRUE),
               max(oc$season.precip.spring, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = 100)

pred_precip <- as.data.frame(emmeans(cool_model_fig, ~ season.precip.spring,
                                     at = list(season.precip.spring = sp_grid)))

fig_precip <- ggplot(pred_precip, aes(x = season.precip.spring, y = emmean)) +
  geom_point(data = oc, aes(x = season.precip.spring, y = mean_overlap, colour = site),
             inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 1.8) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), alpha = 0.18, fill = "grey60") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.3, colour = "black") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = site_colors, labels = site_labels, name = "Ecosystem") +
  labs(x = "Cool-season precipitation (mm)",
       y = "Co-flowering synchrony") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 20) +
theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# ---- (B) PDO (linear) ----
pdo_grid <- seq(min(oc$annual.PDO, na.rm = TRUE),
                max(oc$annual.PDO, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = 100)

pred_pdo <- as.data.frame(emmeans(pdo_model_fig, ~ annual.PDO,
                                  at = list(annual.PDO = pdo_grid)))

fig_pdo <- ggplot(pred_pdo, aes(x = annual.PDO, y = emmean)) +
  geom_point(data = oc, aes(x = annual.PDO, y = mean_overlap, colour = site),
             inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 1.8) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), alpha = 0.18, fill = "grey60") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.3, colour = "black") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = site_colors, labels = site_labels, name = "Ecosystem") +
  labs(x = "Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO)",
       y = "Co-flowering synchrony") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 20) +
theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# ---- Stacked two-panel figure: cool precip (top), PDO (bottom), shared legend ----
fig_climate <- ggpubr::ggarrange(fig_precip, fig_pdo,
                                 ncol = 1, labels = c("(A)", "(B)"),
                                 font.label = list(size = 18, face = "bold"),
                                 common.legend = TRUE, legend = "bottom")

fig_climate
ggsave("figures/FIGURE2_synchrony_climate.svg", fig_climate, width = 7, height = 10)
ggsave("figures/FIGURE2_synchrony_climate.png", fig_climate, width = 7, height = 10, dpi = 300)
```

```{r}
# OVERLAP ONLY PLOT

  labs(x = expression("Year")) +
```

###Supplemental- does spring precip or PDO change over time
```{r}

# --- Yearly climate series: one value per year (averaged over sites where they differ) ---
clim_year <- oc_cc %>%
  dplyr::group_by(year) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(spring_precip = mean(season.precip.spring, na.rm = TRUE),
                   pdo           = mean(annual.PDO,           na.rm = TRUE),
                   .groups = "drop")

# --- Linear trend tests ---
precip_trend <- lm(spring_precip ~ year, data = clim_year)
pdo_trend    <- lm(pdo ~ year,           data = clim_year)
summary(precip_trend)   # slope + p: is cool-season precip changing over time?
summary(pdo_trend)      # slope + p: is PDO changing over time?
#no climate change over time

clim_theme <- theme_classic(base_size = 18) +
  theme(text        = element_text( face = "bold"),
        axis.text   = element_text( face = "bold", size = 13, colour = "black"),
        axis.title  = element_text( face = "bold", size = 18),
        axis.line   = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 1.2))

# --- (A) Cool-season precip over time ---
precip_time <- ggplot(clim_year, aes(x = year, y = spring_precip)) +
  geom_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +                  
  geom_point(colour = "black", size = 2) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Cool-season precipitation (mm)") +
  clim_theme

# --- (B) PDO over time ---
pdo_time <- ggplot(clim_year, aes(x = year, y = pdo)) +
  geom_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(colour = "black", size = 2) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Annual PDO index") +
  clim_theme

# --- Combine (stacked) ---
clim_time_fig <- ggpubr::ggarrange(precip_time, pdo_time, ncol = 1,
                                   labels = c("(A)", "(B)"),
                                   font.label = list(size = 18, face = "bold"))
clim_time_fig
ggsave("figures/FIGURES_climate_over_time.svg", clim_time_fig, width = 14, height = 12)
ggsave("figures/FIGURES_climate_over_time.png", clim_time_fig, width = 14, height = 12, dpi = 300)
```
